display.title: Episode 406: The Stargazer (Parshas Vayeitzei)
display.summary_short: Yaakov's ladder as the ladder of prayer, two young guests say the Shema, and a stargazer learns that tzedakah is stronger than the stars.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Parshas Vayeitzei 5750. Uncle Yossi tells of Yaakov Avinu's dream of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels going up and then down. Why up first? The Zohar, by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, explains that the ladder is davening: the words of our tefillos become angels that climb up to Hashem, and Hashem's blessings come back down the same ladder. So we should daven clearly and carefully, and with joy, trusting that Hashem listens. After the Hakochainik march, a brother and sister visiting with their father recite the Shema and the first pasuk of the Torah, one of the Twelve Pesukim, and everyone gives tzedakah. The story: a stargazer whom nobody believes predicts that a young man walking into the forest will not come out alive. The young man returns cheerful, and when asked what happened, recalls sharing his bread with a starving old man, at which moment a snake slipped out of his sack. The stargazer concludes that the kindness overpowered the stars. As Shlomo HaMelech wrote, tzedakah saves from death. The show ends with a sponsor message and candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Daven carefully and joyfully, because our prayers climb up to Hashem; and tzedakah is so powerful that it saves from death.
